title: Basic Laboratory Safety
description: Learn essential safety rules for working in a chemistry laboratory.
passageText: Laboratory safety is the first rule of any experiment. Always wear safety goggles to protect your eyes. A lab coat protects your clothes and skin. Never taste or smell chemicals directly. Read the label on every bottle before use. Keep flammable materials away from open flames. Clean spills immediately. Know the location of the fire extinguisher and the emergency shower. Report all accidents to your supervisor immediately.

title: Simple Distillation
description: Understand how distillation separates liquid mixtures.
passageText: Distillation is a process that separates liquids based on their boiling points. The mixture is heated in a flask. The component with the lower boiling point evaporates first. The vapor travels through a condenser, where cool water flows around the outside. The vapor cools and condenses back into liquid. The pure liquid is collected in a receiving flask. This method is used to purify water and separate alcohol from water.

title: Chemical Reaction Rates
description: Understand what factors affect the speed of chemical reactions.
passageText: Reaction kinetics studies how fast chemical reactions occur. Temperature has a major effect: higher temperatures increase molecular movement and collision frequency, speeding up reactions. Catalysts accelerate reactions without being consumed. Concentration also matters because more reactant particles lead to more collisions. Surface area is important for solid reactants; smaller particles react faster. Pressure affects gas-phase reactions significantly. Engineers optimize these factors to maximize yield and minimize cost in industrial processes.

title: Process Control Systems
description: Learn how chemical plants maintain safe and efficient operations.
passageText: Process control systems maintain variables like temperature, pressure, and flow rate at desired setpoints. Sensors measure the current value of each variable. A controller compares the measurement to the setpoint and calculates the required adjustment. The final control element, typically a valve, adjusts the process. Feedback control loops continuously correct deviations. Distributed control systems allow operators to monitor entire plants from a central control room. Safety instrumented systems automatically shut down processes when dangerous conditions are detected.

title: Chemical Reactor Design
description: Explore the principles behind industrial reactor selection and design.
passageText: Reactor design is central to chemical engineering. Batch reactors process materials in discrete quantities and are suitable for small-scale or multi-product plants. Continuous stirred-tank reactors maintain uniform composition throughout and operate at steady state. Plug-flow reactors move material through a tube with minimal back-mixing, achieving high conversion. Fluidized-bed reactors suspend solid catalyst particles in upward-flowing gas, providing excellent heat transfer. Engineers select reactor type based on reaction kinetics, heat transfer requirements, and economic factors.
